content.title: About
content.content: Pina Colada is a ready‑to‑drink cocktail mix based on pineapple juice, coconut cream, and rum (non‑alcoholic version without rum). It has a sweet tropical flavor, creamy texture, and a strong aroma of pineapple and coconut.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pina Colada was officially declared the national drink of Puerto Rico in 1978.
The first recipe appeared in the 1950s at the Caribe Hilton bar in San Juan.
A non‑alcoholic version is widely used in kids' menus and venues where alcohol is prohibited.
The mixture can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 7 days without losing flavor or aroma.
Pina Colada is often served in a highball glass with a pineapple wedge and a cherry.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Pineapple juice is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Coconut cream provides potassium, important for fluid balance and muscle function.

items.title: Quick Energy
items.content: Sugars from pineapple and coconut give a fast source of glucose for an energy boost.

items.title: Bromelain
items.content: Pineapple contains the enzyme bromelain, which aids digestion and reduces inflammation.

items.title: Hydration Support
items.content: The water content in the juice and coconut cream helps maintain body hydration.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: The sweet taste comes from added sugars, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Coconut Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut cream.

items.title: Caloric Density
items.content: Coconut cream and pineapple juice make the drink relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Alcohol Content in Traditional Recipe
items.content: Classic Pina Colada contains rum; non‑alcoholic versions omit it, but always check the label if total abstinence is required.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Pina Colada chilled, often over ice, in a tall glass. Garnish with pineapple chunks, a cherry, or a sprinkle of toasted coconut. The non‑alcoholic version works as a refreshing summer drink and as a base for dessert cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the ready‑to‑drink mix in a sealed container in the refrigerator for no more than 5‑7 days. If frozen, sugar may crystallize; gently thaw and stir before serving.
